skill.name: ui-design
skill.description: Create editable UI screens in UX Pilot, review them on a shared canvas, and implement selected designs with your project components and design tokens. Requires a connected UX Pilot MCP server and account.
skill.summary: Review editable UX Pilot screens before implementing them in your project.
skill.author: uxpilot-ai

security_audit.summary: The backtick matches are Markdown, and the reconnaissance matches describe React generation and plan limits. The three URL matches configure a documented third-party connection with account access. The workflow can send project content before explicit disclosure approval and relay unverified upgrade links; no evidence of malicious intent or audit-manipulation instructions was found.

remediation.issue: Project content can reach UX Pilot before disclosure approval.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact brief or HTML payload before the first tool call that sends it. Replace sensitive values with placeholders and obtain explicit consent for the transfer.

remediation.issue: Setup registers an authenticated third-party MCP server.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users how to verify the endpoint through official UX Pilot documentation, review the requested account permissions, and remove the connection when no longer needed.

remediation.issue: The workflow forwards unverified upgrade links.
remediation.suggestion: Summarize service errors and direct users to the billing page reached from their signed-in account. Do not endorse a link supplied in a tool response without verifying its destination.

content.user_title: Design and Build UI Screens with UX Pilot
content.value_statement: Changing a layout after implementation can mean rewriting components. This skill puts editable designs on a UX Pilot canvas for review before rebuilding them with your project components.
actual_capabilities: Build a design brief from project routes, copy, brand assets, and design tokens.
Generate mobile or desktop screens with UX Pilot after confirming the design run.
Draft HTML and import it into an editable canvas, then apply targeted revisions.
Share canvas previews and address reported contrast, clipping, and touch target issues.
Rebuild selected screens with existing project components and compare the result with the design preview.
limitations: Requires a UX Pilot account and a configured MCP connection. Briefs and imported HTML are sent to UX Pilot.
UX Pilot design runs may use credits. HTML imports and edits count toward the weekly allowance on the free plan.
The free plan does not return HTML for screens generated by UX Pilot. Rebuilding from a preview may not match exactly.
Visual comparison of the implementation depends on access to a runnable preview and a screenshot tool.

use_cases.title: Review a new product flow
use_cases.description: Compare editable onboarding screens on a canvas before deciding what to build.

use_cases.title: Refine a dashboard layout
use_cases.description: Adjust the hierarchy and spacing of a dashboard while keeping the existing brand and checking for contrast issues.

use_cases.title: Implement a reviewed screen
use_cases.description: Translate a selected design into responsive code using the project component library and design tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a single screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore a layout before changing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a desktop settings page for [product]. Show me the brief before sending it to UX Pilot. Share the canvas link and stop before editing the project.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign an existing page
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a page while preserving the current brand.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [route] and propose a mobile redesign using our existing colors and typography. Use sample data. Ask before sending the brief to UX Pilot.

prompt_templates.title: Import and refine an HTML design
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a canvas design without a credit-based generation run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft HTML for [screen] using placeholder content. Show me what will be shared before importing it into UX Pilot. Check for clipped text, low contrast, and small touch targets.

prompt_templates.title: Implement and verify an approved design
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a reviewed screen in an existing application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the approved [screen] from [canvas link] in [route]. Reuse our components and tokens. Add loading, empty, and error states, then compare screenshots with the design.

output_examples.input: Preview a mobile onboarding flow without changing project files.
output: The canvas contains two editable screens: account setup and notification preferences.
Choose whether to ask for notifications during setup or after the first visit.

output_examples.input: Build the approved dashboard using the existing project components.
output: The dashboard uses the shared filter controls and table component.
The page includes loading, empty, and error states.
The desktop layout matches the canvas preview. The filters stack on narrow screens.

best_practices: Specify the audience, target device, required actions, and brand constraints in the brief.
Review the exact brief or HTML before approving its transfer to UX Pilot.
Choose the screens to implement after reviewing the canvas and its design checks.
anti_patterns: Including credentials, private customer records, or confidential metrics in a design brief or HTML import.
Starting a credit-based run without confirming the cost and obtaining user approval.
Pasting generated HTML directly into the project instead of reusing its components and tokens.

faq.question: What do I need to get started?
faq.answer: You need a UX Pilot account and a configured UX Pilot MCP connection in your assistant.

faq.question: Can I review the design before code changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shares an editable canvas link before implementation. Ask it to stop after sharing the preview if you want design work only.

faq.question: Can I use the canvas without spending design credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask the assistant to draft and import HTML instead of running UX Pilot design generation. Free accounts have a weekly import and edit allowance.

faq.question: What project data is shared with UX Pilot?
faq.answer: The design brief or imported HTML is sent to UX Pilot. Ask to review it first and replace sensitive details with placeholders.

faq.question: Can I implement a design on the free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. You can rebuild from the preview or from HTML you imported. Reading HTML for a screen generated by UX Pilot requires a paid plan.

faq.question: Does it work with an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses your existing components and tokens where they fit and adds new ones only where needed.
